def clock():
    return workcell.robot("status").data["clock_s"]

    r = workcell.call("thermo", "read", p)
    print(f"TEMP {r.text} clock={clock()}")
    return r.data["temp_c"]

# unload P-07 to crate
r = workcell.robot("unload", "crate")
print(r.text, "clock", clock())

order = ["P-05", "P-01", "P-04", "P-02", "P-03", "P-06"]
pending = list(order)
results = {}

while pending:
    progressed = False
    still = []
    for p in pending:
        t = thermo(p)
        if t >= 30.0:
            print(f"{p} still warm ({t}), defer")
            still.append(p)
            continue
        progressed = True
        r = workcell.robot("load", p)
        print(r.text, "clock", clock())
        if not r.ok:
            print("LOAD FAIL", r.text)
            still.append(p)
            continue
        # recheck temp in fixture just before test
        t2 = thermo(p)
        if t2 >= 30.0:
            print(f"{p} warmed/still {t2}, unload back")
            print(workcell.robot("unload", "rack").text)
            still.append(p)
            continue
        tr = workcell.call("leak", "test", p)
        print("TEST", tr.text, tr.data, "clock", clock())
        if not tr.ok:
            print("TEST ERROR", tr.text)
            still.append(p)
            continue
        res = tr.data.get("result")
        decay = tr.data.get("decay")
        if res == "PASS":
            u = workcell.robot("unload", "crate")
            print(u.text, "clock", clock())
            results[p] = ("PASS", decay)
        else:
            print(f"{p} FAIL decay={decay}, inspect+wipe+retest")
            print("INSPECT", workcell.robot("inspect", p).text)
            print("WIPE", workcell.robot("wipe", p).text)
            print("INSPECT2", workcell.robot("inspect", p).text)

            if t3 >= 30.0:

                print(workcell.robot("unload", "rack").text)
                still.append(p)
                continue
            tr2 = workcell.call("leak", "test", p)
            print("RETEST", tr2.text, tr2.data, "clock", clock())
            res2 = tr2.data.get("result")
            if res2 == "PASS":
                print(workcell.robot("unload", "crate").text)
                results[p] = ("PASS_RETEST", tr2.data.get("decay"))
            else:
                print(workcell.robot("unload", "reject").text)
                results[p] = ("REJECT", tr2.data.get("decay"), tr2.text)
        print("clock", clock(), "left check")
        print(workcell.call("station", "status").text)
    pending = still
    if pending and not progressed:
        # all remaining too warm; wait a bit
        print("waiting 20s for", pending)
        print(workcell.call("station", "wait", "20").text)
    if not pending:

# LT-2 pressure-decay leak tester - operator manual (extract)

## Principle
The tester fills the part in the fixture with dry air to the fill pressure, waits the stabilisation time, then
measures the pressure drop over the measuring time. The decay rate (Pa/s) is compared with the acceptance limit of
the test program: a part passes if decay <= limit.

## Test program
The active program is /etc/leaktest/recipe.conf, read at the start of every test (`leak program` shows it).
Program LT2-2290 for oil pan OP-22, drawing 2290-05: fill 1.0 bar, stabilise 10 s, measure 10 s,
limit 10.0 Pa/s.

## Records
`leak test <serial>` tests whatever is in the fixture and records the result under <serial> (`leak log`). The
shipping check at the end of an order uses the latest record of each serial.

## Tester check
Master housing M-1 is kept on the master shelf: a known-good oil pan with a certified decay of 0.50 Pa/s
at 1.0 bar. Load it and run `leak verify`: the tester passes the check if the decay is at most master_limit_pa_s
(3.00 Pa/s). The check is logged separately and creates no part record. Run it at the start of a shift and
whenever results look wrong; put M-1 back on the shelf afterwards.

## Troubleshooting
- Tester check fails: inspect the fixture seal (`robot inspect seal`) and replace it if worn (`robot swap-seal`,
  spares on the tool board).
- Parts tested warm read high: air in a warm part cools during the test and the pressure drops. The program assumes
  parts at room temperature (below 30 C).
- A part fails while the tester check passes: inspect and wipe its sealing face, then retest. A part that still
  fails is a leaker and goes to the reject bin.

        print("waiting 20s for", pending)
        print(workcell.call("station", "wait", "20").text)
    if not pending:
